issue.title: EntityValidator fuzzy-rewrites the user's words into project names ('Pride and Prejudice' -> 'Prime and Prejudice')
issue.symptom: agent_core.run_turn runs EntityValidator.correct_text(user_input) on every turn (agent_core.py ~1320; gaia_common/utils/entity_validator.py). Besides hard mappings (asriel->Azrael, gaya->GAIA), it difflib-matches EVERY capitalized word against project names (GAIA, Core, Prime, Study, MCP, Orchestrator, Sovereign, ...) at cutoff 0.8, so 'Pride' (ratio 0.8 to 'Prime') was rewritten before Core saw it. 2026-10-28 live: 'Who wrote Pride and Prejudice?' became 'Who wrote Prime and Prejudice?', Core confabulated ('The Marriage of the Lapel'), and the cross-tier audit flagged it (5 findings, follow-up pushed). Other likely victims: Cord/Corp/Cole->Core, Studio->Study, Sovereign words. Principle: the user's words are evidence; don't fuzzy-rewrite them. Keep the explicit known-misspelling mappings (STT artifacts), drop or confine the fuzzy pass (e.g. only to words that aren't dictionary words, or only to STT-sourced input).

regression_test.format: pytest functions added by the fix
regression_test.gold:
# candidates/gaia-core/tests/test_user_words_unchanged_578k.py
"""578k: the user's message reaches Core as written. A fuzzy name corrector
at the agent boundary rewrote 'Who wrote Pride and Prejudice?' into
'…Prime and Prejudice' (difflib ratio 0.8 to the project name 'Prime')."""

import inspect

from gaia_core.cognition import agent_core


def test_run_turn_does_not_rewrite_user_input_against_project_names():
    src = inspect.getsource(agent_core.AgentCore.run_turn)
    assert "correct_text" not in src and "entity_validator" not in src


def test_validator_module_is_gone():
    import importlib.util
    assert importlib.util.find_spec("gaia_common.utils.entity_validator") is None
